I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's a complete setup:

## Server-side Configuration

**1. Create a bare git repository**
```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

**2. Create a post-receive hook for automatic deployment**

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive`:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
DEPLOY_DIR="/var/www/html"
mkdir -p $DEPLOY_DIR
cd $DEPLOY_DIR
git clone --bare /git/server .git
git config --bool core.bare false
git reset --hard HEAD
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

**3. Set up the web server**

Start a simple Python HTTP server on port 8080:
```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Or use nginx (more production-ready). Create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default`:
```nginx
server {
    listen 8080 default_server;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
```

Then start nginx:
```bash
sudo systemctl start nginx
```

## Client-side Workflow

Once set up, your workflow becomes:
```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-project
cd my-project
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then test:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

**Key points:**
- The bare repository at `/git/server` acts as the central remote
- The `post-receive` hook automatically checks out to `/var/www/html` whenever you push
- The web server serves files from `/var/www/html`
- This is a simple "push-to-deploy" system
